The temperature list task

Unit 1 · Week 6 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor and blank test log. Load exactly four suitable integer temperatures per run.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. The temperature list task

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention and transfer

Success means load four temperatures, display indices/values, find first minimum without min and defend test coverage. This is formative chapter transfer practice. Exact four-input contract guarantees non-empty data before the minimum search.

2. Retrieval: a first occurrence

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and peer explanation

For[-2,4,-5,-5], minimum value-5 at indices 2 and 3, first index 2. Strict < keeps the earlier equal value. Ask learners to retrieve individually then compare. Revisit position versus value if they answer only-5.

3. Loading and displaying four readings

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and guided prediction

Trace input-2,4,-5,-5 into the list. The four accepted integer inputs guarantee length 4 and indices 0..3. Display is a separate traversal after loading. print pairs 0 -2,1 4,2 -5,3 -5. Input validation is outside this core task. Ask learners to mark the two distinct loops.

4. Tests before the minimum search

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent prediction and pair comparison

Expected first minimum indices/values: [-2,4,-5,-5] ->2/-5; [6,3,8,9] ->1/3; [2,2,2,2] ->0/2. Learners predict from requirements before running. Last tied minimum would be 3 in first case, so this catches <=. Support: label indices on paper. Stretch: choose a four-value case whose minimum occurs last, e.g.[3,2,1,0] ->3/0.

5. Finding the first minimum

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling with faded support

This fragment follows the four-input loading code. Start lowest_index 0 at a real element. Strict < changes only for a smaller temperature. For main test, trace best indices 0,0,2,2. Final output 2 -5. If reusing this algorithm for a variable-length list, check empty input before index 0. Support: retain index/value trace columns.

6. Your program and test record

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent implementation and peer feedback

Learners combine loading, display and minimum search without using min. Run all predicted four-reading cases and preserve expected results. Partner challenges a tie-rule or index explanation after individual coding. Support: provide a blank loop skeleton. Stretch: separately test a reusable search with a one-element list and an empty-list guard, distinguishing those from the exactly-four-input interface.

7. Index 2 or the third reading?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

Correct B: index 2 is the third reading for Python zero-based indexing. In[-2,4,-5,-5], first minimum is index 2/value-5. Displaying human position lowest_index+1 is fine, but keep zero-based index internally for access. If several choose A, label indices 0..3 above item numbers 1..4.

8. Exit ticket: defend the evidence

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket and reflection

For[3,1,1,4], first minimum index 1/value 1. Strict < keeps it, while <= returns 2. Equal values test the tie rule and negative values expose an unsafe guessed best value 0. Fixed four inputs ensure non-empty data; reusable search needs a guard. Collect an individual explanation before Week 7 files and reliable input.
